name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 162 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 162 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in South Kashmir launched counter-insurgency operations in multiple villages after terrorist presence was reported, while the Srinagar police chief chaired a high-level security review on intelligence sharing and valley domination. In Manipur, tribal students intensified agitation demanding scholarship releases and a tragic ambulance collision killed a pregnant woman, and a hooch-related fire claimed 17 lives. The Chhattisgarh government recovered a Maoist weapon dump in the Bijapur forests and killed a suspected KCP cadre, and Lateef Bhat was killed in Kulgam. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Sør-Kashmir igangsatte motinsurgente operasjoner i flere landsbyer etter at terrorister ble rapportert til stede, mens politisjefen i Srinagar ledet en høy-nivå sikkerhetsgjennomgang av etterretningsdeling og dominans i dalen. I Manipur intensiverte stamme-studenter protestene for utbetaling av stipender, og en tragisk ulykke der en ambulanse kolliderte førte til at en gravid kvinne døde, mens en brann forårsaket av hjemmelaget sprit tok 17 liv. Regjeringen i Chhattisgarh oppdaget en maoistisk våpenlagring i Bijapur-skogene og drepte en mistenkt KCP-medlem, og Lateef Bhat ble drept i Kulgam. UCDP registrerte 437 dødsfall i kamprelaterte hendelser i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
